title: Suffix Automaton for Linear-Time Substring Indexing: Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Ruby

abstract: We present a Ruby implementation of a suffix automaton that guarantees linear-time construction and linear-time substring queries. The design follows the classic state-splitting technique, preserving the invariant that each state represents an equivalence class of end-positions. We formally prove that the number of states never exceeds $2n-1$ for a source string of length $n$, and that each extension operation runs in amortized constant time. The implementation is fully verified against a suite of unit tests that confirm the theoretical bounds.
